lens: clarity and depth for a curious 15-year-old and an expert at once
round1Followup: Most round-1 fixes landed: the Transformer is now named (L1009, L1030); the sterile candle goes out at 17 years (L0521); the fiddly-nets candle goes out (L0831); the scale and recipe candles are spoken (L1112, L1116); top-5 and ImageNet are explained (L0712, L0802, L0822); back-propagation is named (L0508); Fodor and Pylyshyn are voiced (L0523); convolution, weights, dropout, the colour split, 'steps', AlexNet's name, the two halves of the Transformer, move 37, RLHF, L1307, L1405, L1503 and L1506 are all fixed. Still open: the word budget, which got worse (3,227 to 3,431), and the residual lane, which is still visual only (an acceptable choice). New problems are listed below.
critical: WORD BUDGET: the narration is 3,431 words against a 3,040 target, 13% over and 204 words more than round 1. A slow voice at about 95 wpm gives roughly 36 minutes of speech before any music holds, so the 32-minute film does not fit. The clarity fixes below add about 120 words, so cut about 450 elsewhere. Candidates: compress the ch15-s05 montage L1522-L1526 (about 75 words) to about 45; L1219 stampede list; merge L0610/L0620/L0611 into one sentence; L1305-L1306; L1412+L1414 into one line; L0902 auction detail; trim L0104/L0105; L1202-L1203; L0212+L0222 into one sentence; L1031 (its caveats are on screen); L0825 second sentence. Keep every line that defines a mechanism.

The two foundations of the whole story are never put into words. (a) WHAT A KNOB IS: 'knobs' first appears in L0213 ('its knobs turned by an autopilot') and again in L0307/L0308, but nobody says a knob sets how strongly one wire counts. 'Weights' is first used in L0703 ('good starting weights') and only defined in ch08 L0809. Fix L0307: 'an eye, random wires, and on each wire a knob, how strongly that wire counts, turned by motors. Knobs, we call them weights.' Then L0809 can say simply 'Sixty million weights in all.' (b) EXCLUSIVE-OR is never defined aloud. Ch04 L0401 says only 'Four lanterns. The lit two sit on opposite corners.' Yet L0509's payoff ('until it learns exclusive-or by itself') and the 17-year sterile candle depend on it. Fix L0401: 'A puzzle called exclusive-or: light up if one input is on, but not both. Four lanterns; the lit two sit on opposite corners.'

Training as 'downhill' is never tied to the error, and step size is never set up, though both deep dives rely on them. L0510 'Learning is a walk downhill in fog' does not say WHAT the hill is. The shot animates timid and bold strides, but the narration never mentions stride, so L0819's 'Three times, they shortened their steps by hand' pays off a setup the ear never got. Fix L0510: 'Each tug moves the knobs a little downhill, toward less error. But the walk is in fog: a hollow can look like the bottom, and too timid a step gets trapped.' (claim e4-rhw; mechanics in bible §AlexNet / ch05 staging).

Hinton joining Google is never spoken, so L1304 ('He had left Google to speak freely') refers to an employer the ear never heard. L0902 auctions 'his tiny company' but never says who won. Per e8-auction, he chose Google. Fix L0902: '...from a laptop on a wastebasket. He stopped at forty-four million dollars, and chose Google.' (Cut 'auctioned ... by email' wording to stay within budget.)

issues.problem: The candle-clock, the film's central device for 'what people believed and for how long', is never explained aloud. The ear has to work out from L0209 and L0219 that a candle is a belief and that its burn time is how long the belief held. A listener who glances away from the screen misses the rule that the whole film is built on.
issues.fix: L0111: 'Below them, a shelf of candles. Each is a belief, and it burns as long as people held it. A few are still burning.' (+10 words)

issues.problem: 'Almost nobody could teach the second layer' comes before 'hidden layer' is introduced, and the ear was never told that the Mark I's random wires (L0307) never learned. In L0403, 'Two cuts can: a hidden layer' uses the term as an appositive without saying what it is.
issues.fix: L0320: 'Its random wires never learned; only the last knobs did. Almost nobody could teach a layer in the middle.' L0403: 'Two cuts can, made by a middle row of lanterns that neither sees nor answers: a hidden layer. Nobody in the mainstream knew how to train one.' (claims e2-mark1-random, e2-exits)

issues.problem: 'the combinatorial explosion' is quoted and never explained. A 15-year-old hears jargon, and the reason the Lighthill report mattered is lost.
issues.fix: 'Lighthill's report blamed "the combinatorial explosion": possibilities that multiply faster than any machine can search.'

issues.problem: 'doubting these nets could even tell one piece from two' is cryptic. Was it one object or two, a piece of what? This is the dissenter's actual position and should be clear.
issues.fix: '...doubting these nets could even tell whether a shape was in one piece or two.'

issues.problem: 'At the top, the error glows' skips the step that makes error meaningful: the net's answer is compared with the right one.
issues.fix: 'Light flows up; at the top, the answer is checked against the right one, and the error glows.'

issues.problem: The belief that AlexNet ended (TO SEE, A MACHINE NEEDS FEATURES DESIGNED BY EXPERTS) is on screen in s01 but never spoken as a belief, and its start date is never said. 'Burned thirteen years' (L0826) then has no audible origin. Per the bible (Era 8, 'How long it lasted') it runs from SIFT, 1999, to 2012. The brief asks 'how long did people think that way': the ear should hear both ends.
issues.fix: L0802: 'The belief of the day, since about 1999: to see, a machine needs stencils cut by experts. Allowed five guesses, the best still missed about one in four.' L0826 can then stand.

issues.problem: The narration says 'Add the nine', but the on-screen sum has six terms (the zero column is omitted). A teenager counting will find six, and an expert will notice the toy 3x3 stencil is not AlexNet's 11x11 colour stencil. The shot carries no ILLUSTRATIVE label, unlike ch10-s06.
issues.fix: Show all nine terms on screen, including the three ×0 terms, and add the label 'ILLUSTRATIVE · AlexNet's real first-layer stencils are 11 × 11, in colour' (claim e8-architecture).

issues.problem: AlexNet's architecture (five stencil layers, then three fully connected layers ending in a thousand answers, e8-architecture) is never said aloud. The cathedral visual builds it, but L0830 'in the great halls' then refers to halls the narration never introduced.
issues.fix: L0809: 'Ninety-six stencils in the first layer; four more layers stencil those: edges, textures, parts, things. Then three great halls, where every lantern sees everything, end in a thousand doors, one per answer.'

issues.problem: 'it trained six times faster' still reads as AlexNet itself; the claim (e8-ingredients) is a four-layer test net on CIFAR-10. The reason the weir helps is also missing, though the film has a ready payoff: the fading whisper (L0613).
issues.fix: 'The below-zero rule is a weir: it never squashes a strong signal, so the messenger's tug stays strong. In their test, six times faster.' (confirm the non-saturation rationale is in the bible's AlexNet section before voicing it; otherwise keep only 'In their test').

issues.problem: Dropout is shown but its purpose is never said, so a teenager hears vandalism, not a cure for memorising.
issues.fix: '...snuffed half the lanterns at random, each time, so no lantern could lean on another.'

issues.problem: 'Their professor couldn't sit, so couldn't fly' is a riddle; the bad back is never mentioned, and the line also sets up 'a man who will not sit' in ch09.
issues.fix: 'Their professor's bad back meant he couldn't sit, so couldn't fly.'

issues.problem: Where the three cards come from is still unsaid. The ear was never told that each word enters as a list of numbers, and 'All three are learned' doesn't say how. The link back to 1986, which an expert expects and a teen enjoys, is missing.
issues.fix: 'Each word arrives as a list of numbers. From it, three cards: a question... All three made by learned settings, tuned by the same messenger from 1986.'

issues.problem: 'Records.' Records at what? That it was built for translation is only said later (L1031).
issues.fix: 'Records in translation, English to German and to French.' (e10-results)

issues.problem: 'Its curtain hides the words to come' uses a curtain the ear never met. The masked self-attention mechanism, where each word may look only backward, is the key point and is carried by the visual alone.
issues.fix: 'The writing half wears a curtain: each word may look back, never ahead.' Then L1033's question follows.

issues.problem: 'Florence's slip glints. They had mostly to wait.' L0828 filed the Florence prophecy 'in the file', but here it is a 'slip' on a wall. By ear this is a riddle.
issues.fix: 'Remember Florence: just wait for faster chips and bigger data. Mostly, they only had to wait.'

issues.problem: 'An octopus on a cable' is a thought experiment with no owner and no frame. A teenager will be lost. The authors' names are on screen only.
issues.fix: 'At the rim, two linguists told a parable: an octopus tapping an undersea cable learns the shape of words, never their meaning.' (e11-octopus)

issues.problem: 'One author of the stochastic parrots paper' names a paper the ear has never heard of and leaves the author unnamed. Gebru is then named first in L1310.
issues.fix: 'Timnit Gebru, who co-wrote a paper on the risks of ever-larger language models, left Google. She says she was fired; Google says she resigned.'

issues.problem: 'Of the three Turing laureates' uses a term never introduced aloud; the 2018 award appears on screen only in ch15-s06. A teenager won't know who 'the three' are.
issues.fix: 'The three who shared computing's highest prize for these networks? Two signed. LeCun did not.' (e9-turing, e12-three-camps)

issues.problem: 'A small price tag on a vast building' comes before DeepSeek is named, so the ear doesn't know whose price or what building.
issues.fix: L1406: 'December 2024: DeepSeek's V3 model, with a small price tag: about five and a half million dollars.' L1407: 'Its own sum for one final run: not the research, not the chips.'

issues.problem: L1408 says 'a reasoning model' before ch15 L1503 explains what one is. In L1410, 'Compute doesn't matter? A struck match' voices a belief that was never lit or attributed, so it plays as a rhetorical question.
issues.fix: L1408: 'Then DeepSeek released a model that reasons step by step before answering, open to all.' L1410: 'For a day, some concluded compute didn't matter: a struck match, out within a day. But the one-to-three-years candle went out too, after two years.'

issues.problem: 'alleged copying' is looser than the claim (e13-distillation), which is distillation: training on another model's answers through fraudulent accounts. The Chinese commerce ministry's defence that it is 'a common practice' is on screen but not spoken, so the spoken side is uneven.
issues.fix: 'Anthropic and US agencies alleged Chinese labs trained on American models' answers; Beijing called it a smear, and said the practice is common.'

issues.problem: Whose phone rings is never said; 'shared with the man from Versailles' implies but does not name the laureate.
issues.fix: 'Two in the morning, October 2024. The tall man's phone rings.'

issues.problem: 'Under a microscope' doesn't say whose. The study is Anthropic's own, of its own model (e14-biology). For even-handedness, since OpenAI and DeepSeek are named in L1521, the narration should name the lab, as the screen label does.
issues.fix: 'Looking inside their own model, Anthropic's researchers found it chose "rabbit" before writing the line.'

issues.problem: 'One lantern is still dark' is the film's last open question, and the narration never says what it is. The screen carries 'How, exactly, does it reach its answer?' and Anthropic's 'about a quarter' quote. A teenager leaves without the question the film wants to spark.
issues.fix: 'One lantern is still dark: how, exactly, it reaches its answers.'

issues.problem: The gold-rush era has no spoken belief, though the bible (Era 9) gives one: 'the AlexNet recipe works everywhere'. AlphaGo's mechanics also get no words (a net proposes moves, a net judges the board, search). This is acceptable under the word budget, but it is the one era where 'what people believed' is missing.
issues.fix: Optional, if the cuts allow: in ch09-s03, 'The new belief: the recipe from Florence works on everything.' Otherwise leave it.

issues.problem: 'set a record' doesn't say on what.
issues.fix: '...set a record on handwritten digits, with no warm-up.' (e7-ciresan)

issues.problem: IDs are still out of order within shots: L0222 after L0212, L0520/L0521 after L0509, L1421 before L1418, L1527 between L1513 and L1514, L1528 after L1502.
issues.fix: Confirm that narration and timeline use array order, or renumber before film-narrate.

strengths: The AlexNet deep dive is now complete and teachable for both audiences. It goes from photo-as-numbers (150,528) to a worked stencil sum, names convolution, then covers stacking, stencils learned from noise by the 1986 messenger, ReLU and pooling, the 10-bit label against 60 million weights (with 'memorise' named), crops, mirrors and dropout, the unbidden colour/greyscale GPU split, and the hand-cut learning rate. The result is stated honestly: top-5 explained, a 7-net ensemble, best single network near 18%, and credit to IDSIA.

The Transformer sequence is the best teaching in the film. The slow reader and fading whisper motivate it, attention arrives from translation, and the doubted lunch idea comes next. Q/K/V are given as question, label and message, with a correctly worked softmax (2,0,4,2 → halve → about half to river). 'Why divide by eight' is paid off exactly (d_k = 64), followed by eight heads, the position clock face, talk-then-think ×6, why it won (one huge multiplication), its n² cost, the 'not first, not only, built to translate' caveats, and the decoder-only curtain leading into next-word prediction.

The candle clock answers the brief's 'how long did people think that way' throughout: 16, about 7, 17, about 7, 15-ish, 13, 20, 2 and 2 years, and one day. L1515 honestly notes that the newest candles haven't finished burning.

Dissent is voiced in every era: Gerard at the first rim, Minsky at the second, Amari and Linnainmaa's lit windows in the winter, Fodor and Pylyshyn's systematicity ('still argued'), LeCun's 'couldn't get our papers published', IDSIA against the warm-up belief, Bender, Koller, Gebru and Marcus against scale, the three lamps of 2023, and the three-voice gap debate in 2026.

Payoffs across decades reward attentive viewers: Buffalo's mail, pre-training 'in a different coat', Cyc's 'practically nothing from raw text' against GPT-2's objective, Rosenblatt's 1961 sentence sixty-one years early, Widrow's 'remember him', Hopfield's forgotten talk remembered by the Nobel, and the jug of light reused for next-word sampling.

Fairness reflexes are strong: backprop credit is shared and Hinton's own disclaimer quoted, 'one book's fault? historians still argue', Gebru's fired/resigned, Anthropic's FTX money, Pentagon dispute and $1.5B settlement, OpenAI's incident with an outside sceptic, Amodei labelled a rival, and DeepSeek's cost in its own terms.
